questions.d: A money-back guarantee to reduce purchase risk

questions.question: An e-commerce brand adds star ratings to product pages and sees a 9% lift in add-to-cart rate. However, products with fewer than 5 reviews see no lift. What explains this, and what is the fix?
questions.a: Products with few reviews have lower prices — bundle them with higher-rated products
questions.b: Below a social proof threshold, sparse reviews reduce credibility rather than building it — hide review counts below 5 and instead display bestseller badges or "X people bought this" signals until reviews accumulate
questions.c: The star rating widget is not rendering correctly on mobile for low-review products — fix the CSS
questions.d: Low-review products have worse descriptions — improve copy to compensate for lack of reviews

questions.question: A B2B SaaS product page has a 1.4% demo request rate. Social proof includes a generic "Trusted by thousands" badge and three short testimonials. What evidence-based restructuring would most improve conversion?
questions.a: Remove all social proof to reduce page clutter and focus on the CTA
questions.b: Replace generic claims with specific, named customer proof — logo wall of ICP logos, quantified outcome quotes ("cut reporting time by 60%"), and a G2 review widget — placing the strongest proof adjacent to the CTA
questions.c: Add a video testimonial autoplay reel above the fold to maximise time-on-page
questions.d: Increase the size of the "Trusted by thousands" badge and add an animated counter

questions.question: Lead scoring combines two types of data. Which pair correctly describes them?
questions.a: Traffic source and time on site
questions.b: Demographic / firmographic fit (explicit) and behavioural engagement (implicit)
questions.c: Lead volume and close rate by channel
questions.d: Campaign spend and cost per lead

questions.question: MQLs passed from marketing convert to pipeline at only 8%, far below the 25% target. What is the most likely scoring model problem?
questions.a: The MQL threshold is too high — lower it so more leads are passed to sales
questions.b: The model is over-weighting engagement signals like email opens, which inflate scores for unqualified contacts — it needs to weight fit criteria (title, company size, industry) more heavily
questions.c: Marketing needs to send more nurture emails before passing leads so contacts are more warmed up
questions.d: Sales needs better discovery training to convert the leads they are receiving

questions.question: A marketing ops team wants to build a predictive lead score using 10,000 closed-won and closed-lost deals from the past two years. What is the single most important data quality check before building the model?
questions.a: Verify all leads have a complete set of 20+ firmographic fields before including them
questions.b: Ensure the win/loss label is reliable — check for deals marked lost that were actually cancelled, stale deals never properly dispositioned, and recency bias if win rates changed significantly in the past 6 months
questions.c: Confirm the dataset is balanced — downsample won deals to match the number of lost deals before training
questions.d: Remove all deals under $5K ACV since they are not representative of the target market

questions.question: The "content distribution" step in a content marketing workflow refers to what?
questions.a: Deciding which team member writes each piece of content
questions.b: Actively getting published content in front of the right audience through owned, earned, and paid channels
questions.c: Tracking how content ranks in search results after publication
questions.d: Repurposing long-form content into shorter formats

questions.question: A B2B content team publishes two posts per week but organic traffic has plateaued. Distribution is limited to the blog and one LinkedIn post. What is the highest-leverage distribution expansion?
questions.a: Increase production to four posts per week to compound SEO gains faster
questions.b: Audit existing content for quick SEO wins, then build a multi-channel distribution workflow: LinkedIn native posts, newsletter syndication, community sharing, and employee amplification — more distribution from fewer new pieces
questions.c: Launch a paid content syndication campaign to drive traffic to existing posts
questions.d: Repurpose every post into a Twitter/X thread to reach a new audience

questions.question: A content programme has 200+ published assets. 80% of traffic goes to 12% of posts. The team produces 8 new posts per month. What resource allocation maximises content ROI?
questions.a: Continue at the same production rate — new posts compound into traffic over 12-18 months
questions.b: Stop all new production until all existing content is audited and refreshed
questions.c: Shift 40-50% of production budget to updating and redistributing high-performing content, build topical clusters around the top 12% to capture related keyword demand, and use the remaining budget on new posts targeting identified gaps
questions.d: Delete all posts in the bottom 88% of traffic to concentrate site authority

questions.question: Net Revenue Retention (NRR) above 100% means what for a SaaS business?
questions.a: The company has more new customers than churned customers this period
questions.b: Revenue from existing customers is growing — expansion revenue exceeds churn and contraction combined
questions.c: The company's gross margin is above 100%, indicating negative COGS
questions.d: All customers renewed their contracts with no downgrades

questions.question: A company has 120% NRR and 15% logo churn. What does this combination tell you, and what risk does it reveal?
questions.a: The business is healthy with no risks — high NRR more than compensates for any churn
questions.b: Revenue is growing from existing accounts but the company is losing a significant number of customers — likely smaller accounts churn while large accounts expand, creating concentration risk and masking acquisition problems
questions.c: The NRR calculation is incorrect — NRR cannot exceed 100% if logo churn is above 5%
questions.d: The 15% logo churn is within normal SaaS range and the 120% NRR indicates strong product-market fit across all segments

questions.question: A CFO wants to improve NRR from 105% to 120% within 12 months without increasing headcount. Which lever combination has the highest expected impact on NRR specifically?
questions.a: Launch a new product tier priced 40% above current plans and migrate all customers to it
questions.b: Build a usage-based expansion trigger (automated upsell prompt at 80% of plan limit), launch a QBR programme for accounts over $10K ARR focused on expansion, and introduce a formalised churn save playbook with win-back offers for at-risk accounts
questions.c: Focus all CS resources on onboarding new customers faster so they expand earlier
questions.d: Reduce prices by 20% to improve retention rates, which will lift NRR

questions.question: What fundamentally distinguishes ABM from broad demand generation?
questions.a: ABM uses only outbound channels while demand gen uses only inbound
questions.b: ABM targets specific high-value accounts with personalised programmes rather than casting a wide net to generate leads in bulk
questions.c: ABM is only for enterprise companies; demand gen is for SMB and mid-market
questions.d: ABM measures success by MQL volume; demand gen measures by pipeline value

questions.question: An ABM programme targets 200 enterprise accounts. After 6 months, pipeline from target accounts is low despite high impression share. Sales says engagement is low. What is the most likely problem?
questions.a: The target account list is too small — expand to 1,000 accounts
questions.b: The personalisation is too shallow — ads and outreach use only company name substitution without addressing the specific business problem or buying committee stage
questions.c: The ABM platform is not syncing correctly with the CRM — fix the integration before evaluating results
questions.d: ABM requires 12+ months to show pipeline — report back in another 6 months

questions.question: A revenue team debates "1:1 ABM" (highly customised per account) vs "1:many ABM" (personalised by segment). They have 2 enterprise AEs and 1 marketing person for ABM. Which strategy is correct and how should measurement differ from demand gen?
questions.a: 1:many ABM is correct given resource constraints — measure by MQL volume just like demand gen
questions.b: 1:1 ABM is correct for enterprise but should be measured by pipeline created per target account, deal velocity in named accounts, and multi-threaded contact coverage — not by MQL volume or CPL metrics
questions.c: 1:1 ABM is correct and should be measured by total impressions across the target account list
questions.d: Neither — with 1 marketing person ABM is not viable; all resources should go to inbound SEO

questions.question: What is Google Performance Max (PMax)?
questions.a: A bidding strategy that maximises clicks within a fixed daily budget
questions.b: A campaign type that uses Google's AI to serve ads across all Google channels — Search, Display, YouTube, Discover, Gmail, and Maps — from a single campaign
questions.c: A smart keyword tool that automatically adds negative keywords based on search term reports
questions.d: A campaign type limited to Shopping and Display inventory for e-commerce advertisers

questions.question: An advertiser's PMax shows Google-attributed ROAS of 6x, but incrementality testing shows only 2x lift. What most likely explains the gap?
questions.a: PMax has a bug in conversion tracking that double-counts conversions
questions.b: PMax's attribution models over-credit conversions that would have happened anyway — brand searches and retargeting get attributed as PMax-driven even when the touchpoint was not incremental
questions.c: Incrementality testing is not accurate enough for PMax because holdout groups are too small
questions.d: The MTA model is wrong — it underweights Google's role in the customer journey

questions.question: A PMax campaign is cannibalising branded search traffic and the advertiser cannot separate brand from non-brand performance in the campaign report. What is the most effective fix?
questions.a: Pause PMax entirely and run individual campaign types for each channel
questions.b: Add brand terms as negative keywords at the account or campaign level, run a separate brand search campaign to maintain brand coverage, and use campaign-level URL expansion settings to limit PMax landing page choices
questions.c: Lower the PMax target ROAS so the algorithm prioritises non-brand queries naturally
questions.d: Enable all ad extensions so PMax has enough creative signals to differentiate brand from non-brand traffic automatically

questions.question: What does a retention cohort chart measure?
questions.a: Revenue generated by each marketing channel over time
questions.b: The percentage of users from a specific starting period who are still active at each subsequent time interval
questions.c: How long it takes new users to complete their first purchase
questions.d: The lifetime value of customers grouped by acquisition channel

questions.question: A cohort chart shows Day 1 retention of 40% across all cohorts, but Day 30 retention improving from 8% to 18% over 6 months of product changes. What does this pattern indicate?
questions.a: Acquisition quality has improved — newer cohorts are better qualified users
questions.b: Early activation (D1) remains a problem but long-term habit formation is improving — the product changes are working for users who get past the initial drop, but early onboarding still needs fixing
questions.c: The data is inconsistent — D30 retention cannot improve if D1 retention stays flat
questions.d: The product has reached product-market fit, since monthly retention is approaching 20%

questions.question: Two acquisition channels show identical Day 30 retention (22%). However, Channel A customers have 3x higher expansion revenue at Month 6. What is the strategic implication for budget allocation?
questions.a: Split budget equally since retention parity proves both channels deliver equivalent customer quality
questions.b: Channel A delivers customers with higher growth potential — retention alone is an incomplete quality signal, and budget should shift toward Channel A with LTV-to-CAC as the primary allocation metric rather than retention rate
questions.c: Investigate whether Channel A customers are gaming the expansion mechanism before reallocating budget
questions.d: Retention at 30 days is the definitive quality metric — expansion data beyond 30 days is too speculative for budget decisions

questions.question: In Osterwalder's Value Proposition Canvas, what two sides does it map?
questions.a: Product features and pricing tiers
questions.b: Customer Profile (jobs, pains, gains) and Value Map (products, pain relievers, gain creators)
questions.c: Brand positioning and competitive differentiation
questions.d: Marketing channels and customer acquisition costs

questions.question: A B2B product team writes: "Our platform saves time and improves efficiency." Using the Value Proposition Canvas, what is wrong with this statement?
questions.a: It is too long — value propositions should be one word or phrase
questions.b: It addresses gain creators but does not map to a specific customer job or pain — "saves time" is generic and not grounded in a concrete, observable customer struggle
questions.c: It should include pricing to be a complete value proposition
questions.d: It is correct — efficiency and time savings are universally valued and need no further specificity

questions.question: Two competitors offer the same core feature set at the same price. How should a product marketing team use the Value Proposition Canvas to find a defensible differentiation angle?
questions.a: Compete on price — when features and positioning are equivalent, cost is the only differentiator
questions.b: Run customer interviews to deeply map the highest-intensity unsolved pains and unmet gains — find a pain reliever or gain creator the market underserves, and build positioning and product prioritisation around that gap
questions.c: Rewrite messaging to emphasise the company's founding story and values as the differentiator
questions.d: Add more features faster than the competitor to create differentiation through product breadth

questions.question: Research on video ad performance consistently shows the most critical moment for viewer retention is which part?
questions.a: The middle section where the main message is delivered
questions.b: The end card where the CTA is displayed
questions.c: The first 3 seconds — where the hook must stop the scroll
questions.d: The audio track — sound quality predicts completion rate

questions.question: A paid social video ad achieves 65% video completion rate but generates almost no clicks or conversions. What is the most likely creative problem?
questions.a: The video is too short — under 30 seconds cannot build enough trust for a conversion
questions.b: The CTA is buried or appears only at the end — viewers are engaged but the conversion action is not clearly presented at the peak engagement moment
questions.c: The targeting is wrong — high completion rate indicates the wrong audience is watching
questions.d: The landing page is the problem, not the creative — strong completion rates prove the ad is working

questions.question: A DTC brand runs 8 video ad variations and finds one "ugly," unpolished UGC-style video significantly outperforms all polished brand videos on ROAS. How should the creative team respond?
questions.a: The result is an anomaly — polished brand video is required to maintain brand safety and the outlier should be paused
questions.b: The UGC format builds authenticity and trust that polished ads lack here — introduce a systematic UGC production and testing track alongside brand video, using performance data (not aesthetic preference) to guide scaling decisions
questions.c: Replace all brand video production with UGC immediately since the data proves UGC always outperforms
questions.d: Continue running both and report back after the UGC ad fatigues — the win is likely due to novelty

results.title: T-Shaped Strategic Operator
results.description: Broad coverage across the map plus deep spikes and mature business judgement. You diagnose, prioritise and manage trade-offs across the full system.
results.learningPath: Deepen your competitive strategy and GTM leadership muscles. Focus on P&L fluency, cross-functional influence, and org design for marketing functions.

results.title: Full-Stack Marketer
results.description: You confidently connect strategy, channels, analytics, lifecycle and revenue. Strong diagnostic instinct across the system with some gaps in advanced judgement.
results.learningPath: Close your executive-level gaps: prioritisation frameworks, budget allocation under uncertainty, and board-level narrative. Strengthen your weakest domain.

results.title: Functional Generalist
results.description: Good breadth, but depth and judgement are uneven. You know a lot but tend to solve with templates rather than diagnosis.
results.learningPath: Pick your two weakest domains and go deep. Practise diagnostic thinking: when you see a metric problem, ask why at least 3 levels before jumping to a solution.

results.title: Developing Marketer
results.description: You can execute in specific zones but need stronger diagnostic thinking. Building the connective tissue between domains is the key growth lever.
results.learningPath: Prioritise: Analytics & Experimentation + one strategic domain. Learn to read dashboards diagnostically, not just descriptively. Take on a growth experiment end-to-end.

results.title: Tactical Executor
results.description: You recognise individual terms and platforms. The next step is building the system view that connects tools to business outcomes.
results.learningPath: Start with Strategy & Market Thinking fundamentals: JTBD, ICP, value proposition. Then layer in one channel deeply. Understand how each tool connects to a revenue outcome before moving to the next.
